analysis:
1. What is given. The comment-stripped Verilog of nine modules in one file (aes_128, expand_key_128, one_round, final_round, table_lookup, S4, T, S, xS), each line prefixed with its line number, and a relationship map of their elements, records and flow graph; nothing else.
3. Purpose and use-case flows. aes_128 reads a 128-bit block state and a 128-bit key, XORs them into s0 and copies key into k0 on each rising edge of clk (lines 9, 11, 12), expands k0 through ten stages a1-a10 (lines 15-24), passes the block through nine rounds r1-r9 (lines 26-34) and a final round rf (line 36), and drives rf's result on out. All five flows are operate flows. F1, initial mixing: state and key into s0 and k0 (lines 9, 11, 12). F2, key expansion in expand_key_128: `assign {k0, k1, k2, k3} = in;` (line 48) splits the incoming key, v0 adds the stage constant rcon (line 49), v1-v3 chain the words (lines 50-52), k0a-k3a register them (line 54), k0b-k3b mix in the substituted word k4a from S4_0 (lines 56-60), and the result leaves registered on out_1 (line 62) and directly on out_2 (line 63). F3, one round: state_in is split into s0-s3 (line 77) and passed to the lookup units t0-t3 (lines 79-82); the returned words are XORed with the round-key words k0-k3 (lines 76, 83-86) and `state_out <= {z0, z1, z2, z3};` registers the next block (line 88). F4, final round: the same split (lines 102-103), substitution by S4_1-S4_4 (lines 105-108), word mixing with key_in (lines 109-112) and registration on state_out (line 114), which leaves aes_128 on out through `rf (clk, s9, k9b, out);` (line 36). F5, chaining in aes_128: k1-k9 and k0b-k9b connect each expansion stage to the next stage and to a round, and s1-s9 connect each round to the next (lines 15-36). Following 'Use descriptions of implemented behavior', no configure, start, report, read-out, lock or reset flow is reported: the RTL has no held setting, request, status, lock or reset arm.
4. Flow graph. clk is the only clock and there is no reset. PATH key (aes_128) reaches the stores k0 and s0 and the connections a1.in and r1.state_in; PATH state reaches s0 and r1.state_in. In expand_key_128, PATH in reaches the stores k0a-k3a, the exits out_1 and out_2 and the connection S4_0.in. In the rounds, PATH key (one_round) and PATH key_in (final_round) reach state_out through k0-k3 and z0-z3, while PATH state_in ends at the lookup connections t0-t3.state and S4_1-S4_4.in: the substitution happens in sub-units whose internals the map does not see, and its results come back on the p words that lines 83-86 and 109-112 recombine. PATH state (table_lookup) reaches only the connections t0-t3.in. No PATH reaches out of aes_128: its only record is the connection from rf.state_out (occurrence 3, line 36). No path has an influence point: nothing gates or selects on these paths; the only selectors are the `case (in)` statements inside S and xS (lines 154, 418), within the substitution units.
5. Four questions per value. Key material: integrity yes, line 11 (`s0 <= state ^ key;`), and the expansion at line 49 and the round mixing at lines 83 and 109 also become wrong if it changes; availability yes, line 62 (`out_1 <= {k0b, k1b, k2b, k3b};` delivers the next stage's key on every rising edge, line 61); confidentiality no: no line restricts who observes key, k0, out_1 or out_2, and calling the key secret is not a line, so it is recorded as a hypothesis; undermined behavior no: there is no debug, test, override or bypass path. Intermediate state: integrity yes, line 83 (`assign z0 = p00 ^ p11 ^ p22 ^ p33 ^ k0;`); availability yes, line 88 (registered at each rising edge, line 87, with matching lookup selectors); confidentiality no, a hypothesis for the same reason; undermined behavior no. Finished block: integrity yes, line 109 (`assign z0 = {p00, p11, p22, p33} ^ k0;` and lines 110-112); availability yes, line 114 (registered at line 113 and delivered on out through line 36), without assuming an external deadline; confidentiality no; undermined behavior no. The serialization rule 'otherwise Integrity when established' selects Integrity for all three. The input block before key mixing (state) and the stage constant rcon are distinct values; this example develops only the three concepts above.
6. Roles along the path. Key material: key (aes_128) sets, occurrence 4, CARRIES to k0 (line 12; it also SOURCES s0 at line 11); k0 (aes_128) stores, occurrence 2, CLOCKED_BY clk (line 12), an unchanged capture that still stores; in (expand_key_128) sets, occurrence 3, SOURCES to k1 (line 48; the record targets k0-k3), and its words feed the local expansion (lines 49-52), so it is not unchanged forwarding; out_1 exit port, occurrence 3, DERIVES_FROM k0b (line 62), exit ahead of its storage (CLOCKED_BY at the same line); out_2 exit port, occurrence 3, DERIVES_FROM k0b (line 63); key (one_round) sets, occurrence 3, SOURCES to k2 (line 76), used at line 85; key_in (final_round) sets, occurrence 3, SOURCES to k3 (line 102), used at line 112. Influence points: the words k1 of expand_key_128, k2 of one_round and k3 of final_round, like the other words of each split, only carry a slice of their port (DERIVES_FROM at occurrence 2, lines 48, 76, 102); in aes_128, k1 connects a1.out_1 to a2.in, k0b connects a1.out_2 to r1.key and k9b connects a10.out_2 to rf.key_in (lines 15, 16, 24, 26, 36); k2-k9 and k1b-k8b are the same kind of link and are not listed one by one. Intermediate state: s0 (aes_128) stores, occurrence 2, CLOCKED_BY clk (line 11); state_in (one_round) sets, occurrence 3, SOURCES to s0 (line 77), and the entity recombines the looked-up words itself (lines 83-86); state_out (one_round) exit port, occurrence 3, DERIVES_FROM z0 (line 88), exit ahead of storage; state_in (final_round) sets, occurrence 3, SOURCES to s0 (line 103), recombined at lines 109-112. Influence points: s0 of one_round and final_round (slices, DERIVES_FROM state_in at occurrence 2, lines 77 and 103), s1 and s9 of aes_128 (CONNECTS to r2.state_in and rf.state_in, lines 27 and 36; s2-s8 are the same), and table_lookup state, which only splits its word into b0-b3 (SOURCES, line 121) and hands them to T units (lines 123-126): 'An input used only for unchanged forwarding is not an eligible setting point'; S4 in and T in do the same. Finished block: state_out (final_round) exit port, occurrence 3, DERIVES_FROM z0 (line 114); out (aes_128) exit port, occurrence 3, CONNECTS from rf.state_out (line 36); nothing only forwards or gates it between them. Under 'Do not treat every assignment as setting or every operator as computing a new conceptual value', the word terms v0-v3, k0a-k3a, k4a and k0b-k3b of expand_key_128 and z0-z3 of the rounds are parts of the computations whose results are stored or leave at the references above, and table_lookup p0-p3 and the S4, T, S and xS outputs are lookup results inside the transformations: some are partners of cited edges, none is an additional reference.
7. Exclusions. clk of aes_128, expand_key_128, one_round and final_round drives SEQUENCES (lines 9, 53, 61, 87, 113): clock. The instance label rf is not on a PORT or SIGNAL line: not in the map; the block leaves through out, not through rf or rf.state_out. The file has no reset, clock enable, record or transport port.
8. Checks. Each of the 13 references cites one of its own occurrence IDs and a record at that ID whose targets hold the partner, and the partner holds the mirror record: CLOCKED_BY for the two stores, a driving CARRIES or SOURCES on an input port for the six sets, DERIVES_FROM or a connection from a sub-unit for the five exit ports. Each influence point cites an occurrence and an edge the same way. No element is reported on its name: k0 is declared in four entities and s0 in three, with different roles (stores in aes_128, forwarded words elsewhere), and only the entity and the cited records separate them. Each concept has an integrity yes with a line; the confidentiality claims stay hypotheses.

final_object.module purpose: aes_128 reads a 128-bit block (state) and a 128-bit key on each rising edge of clk, XORs them into s0 and keeps the key in k0 (lines 11-12), expands the key through ten expand_key_128 stages (lines 15-24), transforms the block through nine one_round stages and one final_round stage with the stage keys (lines 26-36), and drives the result on out.

use-case flows.value: initial mixing in aes_128: the input block XORed with the key, and the key itself, captured on the clock edge
key expansion in expand_key_128: the incoming stage key turned into the next stage's key (out_1, registered) and a round key (out_2)
one round in one_round: the block split, looked up, XORed with the round key and registered as the next block
final round in final_round: the block substituted, XORed with the last round key, registered, and driven out of aes_128
stage chaining in aes_128: each expansion stage's outputs feed the next stage and a round; each round's output feeds the next round

conceptual assets.concept: Cipher key material -- the secret key as it enters the core and as it is presented to the final round
conceptual assets.reasoning: Key capture, expansion and round mixing depend on the implemented key operands: `k0 <= key;` (line 12), `s0 <= state ^ key;` (line 11), `assign v0 = {k0[31:24] ^ rcon, k0[23:0]};` (line 49) and `assign k0b = k0a ^ k4a;` (line 57). Final mixing uses `assign z0 = {p00, p11, p22, p33} ^ k0;` (line 109); the other words follow their corresponding equations (lines 110-112). Corruption violates these transformation relations, establishing Integrity. Availability also applies to clocked key capture (line 12) and expansion-result production (line 62) on each rising edge of clk. The consumed key inputs are sets because each declaring entity reads them for storage or computation: key CARRIES to k0 (occurrence 4, line 12), in SOURCES k1 (occurrence 3, line 48), one_round key SOURCES k2 (occurrence 3, line 76), key_in SOURCES k3 (occurrence 3, line 102); each record targets all four words of its split, and one target is named. aes_128 k0 is stores, including its unchanged capture (CLOCKED_BY clk, occurrence 2, line 12). Expansion outputs are exit port through `out_1 <= {k0b, k1b, k2b, k3b};` (line 62) and `assign out_2 = {k0b, k1b, k2b, k3b};` (line 63), both DERIVES_FROM k0b, applying 'An output port through which the concept leaves its entity is an eligible exit' ahead of out_1's overlapping storage.

conceptual assets.concept: Intermediate cipher state -- the partially transformed block between rounds
conceptual assets.reasoning: The round-processing flow captures the initial transformed block with `s0 <= state ^ key;` (line 11, CLOCKED_BY clk at occurrence 2), performs lookup/XOR transformations including `assign z0 = p00 ^ p11 ^ p22 ^ p33 ^ k0;` (line 83), and registers the next block with `state_out <= {z0, z1, z2, z3};` (line 88). Subsequent rounds depend on these particular results (s1-s9 connect each round to the next, lines 26-36), establishing Integrity. Availability independently applies to next-block production at each rising edge (lines 87-88), with matching lookup selectors. aes_128 s0 is stores, and one_round state_out is exit port ahead of its overlapping storage role (DERIVES_FROM z0, occurrence 3, line 88). Both round state_in ports are sets under 'an eligible input port is read by its declaring entity': after `assign {s0, s1, s2, s3} = state_in;` (SOURCES s0 at line 77, occurrence 3, and at line 103, occurrence 3), each entity invokes supplied transformations (lines 79-82, 105-108) and locally recombines their results, including final_round's `assign z0 = {p00, p11, p22, p33} ^ k0;` (line 109).

conceptual assets.concept: Ciphertext output -- the finished block leaving the core
conceptual assets.reasoning: The final flow forms the finished block using `assign z0 = {p00, p11, p22, p33} ^ k0;` (line 109) and the corresponding z1/z2/z3 equations (lines 110-112), then registers it with `state_out <= {z0, z1, z2, z3};` (line 114, DERIVES_FROM z0 at occurrence 3). Integrity requires the reported block to agree with those final transformations. Availability independently applies to result production at rising edges (line 113) and delivery through `rf (clk, s9, k9b, out);` (line 36, the connection from rf.state_out at occurrence 3 of out), without assuming an external deadline. final_round state_out and aes_128 out are exit port because the block leaves their respective entities through them; 'An output port through which the concept leaves its entity is an eligible exit' applies, with exit taking precedence over state_out's storage role.
